The task is to rigorously verify W3's coloring pattern $G_{i, j} = i + ((j-1) \bmod 2)$ for the $100 \times 100$ grid.

I will first confirm the number of colors used and then systematically check the constraint for any $2 \times 2$ subgrid based on the parity of the starting column index $j$.

### Verification Steps

**1. Distinct Colors:**
The row index $i$ ranges from $1$ to $100$. The term $((j-1) \bmod 2)$ alternates between 0 (when $j$ is odd) and 1 (when $j$ is even).
*   If $j$ is odd, $G_{i, j} = i$. This generates colors $\{1, 2, \dots, 100\}$.
*   If $j$ is even, $G_{i, j} = i + 1$. This generates colors $\{2, 3, \dots, 101\}$.
The union of these sets is $\{1, 2, \dots, 101\}$. Thus, exactly 101 distinct colors are used.

**2. $2 \times 2$ Constraint Check:**
Consider a $2 \times 2$ subgrid starting at $(i, j)$. The colors are:
$$\begin{pmatrix} G_{i, j} & G_{i, j+1} \\ G_{i+1, j} & G_{i+1, j+1} \end{pmatrix}$$

**Case 1: $j$ is odd.**
$j-1$ is even, so $(j-1) \bmod 2 = 0$. $j$ is odd, so $j \bmod 2 = 1$.
The colors are:
$$\begin{pmatrix} i + 0 & i + 1 \\ (i+1) + 0 & (i+1) + 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} i & i+1 \\ i+1 & i+2 \end{pmatrix}$$
The set of colors is $\{i, i+1, i+2\}$. There are exactly 3 distinct colors. The constraint (at least two squares have the same color) is satisfied.

**Case 2: $j$ is even.**
$j-1$ is odd, so $(j-1) \bmod 2 = 1$. $j$ is even, so $j \bmod 2 = 0$.
The colors are:
$$\begin{pmatrix} i + 1 & i + 0 \\ (i+1) + 1 & (i+1) + 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} i+1 & i \\ i+2 & i+1 \end{pmatrix}$$
The set of colors is $\{i+1, i, i+2\}$. There are exactly 3 distinct colors. The constraint is satisfied.

Since the constraint holds for both cases covering all possible starting columns $j$ (where $1 \le j \le 99$), the verification is complete.

I will now record this finding and submit the report.
